stem: The graph of a hyperbolic function of the form $y=\dfrac{a}{x}+q$ has the horizontal asymptote $y={=q}$. Point A on the graph is at $\left({=x0}, {=y0}\right)$. Calculate the value of $a$.
solution: The horizontal asymptote of $y=\frac{a}{x}+q$ is the line $y=q$. Here the asymptote is $y={=q}$, so $q={=q}$.
Substitute $q={=q}$ and the coordinates of A, $x={=x0}$ and $y={=y0}$, into $y=\frac{a}{x}+q$: ${=y0}=\frac{a}{{=x0}}+{=q}$.
Multiply both sides by ${=x0}$ to clear the fraction: ${=x0}\times{=y0}=\left[\frac{a}{{=x0}}+{=q}\right]\times{=x0}$, so ${=xy}=a+{=qx}$.
notes: Model: ex6-4-2 (A at (-1, 5), q = 3 from the dashed asymptote). The book's figure is replaced by a sentence naming the asymptote, which is exactly what the student reads off the dashed line; no figure is generated. Entry point of the skill: everything positive (a > 0, q > 0, x > 0), the point has whole-number coordinates, and only a is asked, q being read straight from the asymptote. x is never 1 so that 'multiply both sides by x' is never a vacuous step. a = k*x so y is always a whole number; a <= 15.
